source.title: Copolymers at selective interfaces: settled issues and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the general α-copolymer model with α in (0,1), determine the universal weak-coupling slope m_α defined by h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ as λ ↓ 0, where h_c(λ) is the critical curve separating the localized regime L = {(λ,h): F(λ,h) > 0} from the delocalized regime D = {(λ,h): F(λ,h) = 0} and F(λ,h) is the quenched free energy.
accepted.context_brief: Critical slope of the weak-coupling phase boundary

evidence.quote: Highlighted in Figure 2 is the small λ behavior of hc(λ). In fact, as more exten￾sivily explained in section 4, for α ∈ (0,1) we have hc(λ) λ&0 ∼ mαλ, with mα > 0 depending only on α. The slope mα is therefore a universal feature of the model

What the previous results and discussion expose is that a convincing heuristic theory predicting the location of the critical curve, or just its slope at the origin, is lacking. In this sense we consider that capturing the value of mα, for α ∈ (0,1), is an important open problem.

accepted.question_text: For the α = 1/2 copolymer model, prove that the weak-coupling slope m_(1/2) in the asymptotic relation h_c(λ) ~ m_(1/2) λ as λ ↓ 0 is strictly larger than 2/3.
accepted.context_brief: Lower bound on the α = 1/2 critical slope

evidence.quote: Highlighted in Figure 2 is the small λ behavior of hc(λ). In fact, as more exten￾sivily explained in section 4, for α ∈ (0,1) we have hc(λ) λ&0 ∼ mαλ, with mα > 0 depending only on α.
Since computing explicitly quenched quantities may be really out of reach, here are two sub-problems that are open: ? show that m1/2 > 2/3;

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists any α > 0 for which the weak-coupling slope m_α of the critical curve satisfies m_α = 1/(1+α), where h_c(λ) ~ m_α λ as λ ↓ 0.
accepted.context_brief: Exact-formula test for the critical slope

evidence.quote: Highlighted in Figure 2 is the small λ behavior of hc(λ). In fact, as more exten￾sivily explained in section 4, for α ∈ (0,1) we have hc(λ) λ&0 ∼ mαλ, with mα > 0 depending only on α.
Since computing explicitly quenched quantities may be really out of reach, here are two sub-problems that are open: ? show that m1/2 > 2/3; ? is mα = 1/(1+α) for some α > 0?

accepted.question_text: Fix λ > 0 and let h_c(λ) be the critical curve of the copolymer model. The paper proves a smoothing bound of the form F(λ, h_c(λ) + δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ^2 for every δ > 0, where F is the quenched free energy. Can this bound be strengthened by replacing the exponent 2 on δ with a strictly larger exponent?

evidence.quote: for every λ > 0 there exists c(λ) < ∞ such that F(λ,hc(λ) +δ) ≤ (1+α)c(λ)δ2 for every δ > 0.
? Can one improve (20), in the sense of replacing the exponent 2 with a larger value?

accepted.question_text: Let μ(λ,h) be the inverse-correlation-length quantity defined in the localized regime by μ(λ,h) = - lim_(N→∞) (1/N) log E[(1 + exp(-2λ Σ_(n=1)^N (ω_n + h)))/Z_(N,ω)], and let F(λ,h) be the quenched free energy with critical curve h_c(λ). As h approaches h_c(λ) from the localized side, is log μ(λ,h) asymptotic to log F(λ,h)?
accepted.context_brief: Near-critical comparison of μ and free energy

evidence.quote: where µ is defined as µ(λ,h) = − lim N→∞ 1/N log E (1+e−2λ ∑N n=1 (ωn+h))/ZN,ω .

But: ? is it true that logµ(λ,h) ∼ log F(λ,h) as h & hc(λ)? In view of the discussion on disorder relevance in section 1.5, we expect that this is not the case and estab￾lishing such a result would be very interesting.

accepted.question_text: Let Δ_n denote the indicator that the polymer is below the interface at time n, and let P_(N,ω) be the polymer measure. If (λ,h) lies in the interior of the delocalized regime D = {(λ,h): F(λ,h) = 0}, is it true that for every ε > 0 the probability P_(N,ω)(Δ_n = 0 for every n in [εN, N] ∩ ℕ) converges to 0 as N → ∞ for almost every disorder realization ω?

evidence.quote: It is mathematically useful to use the variable ∆n, that in the random walk case is just (1−sign(Sn))/2, i.e. the indicator function that the copolymer is below the axis.
For example: ? Is it true that, if (λ,h) is in the interior of D, for every ε > 0 we have limN→∞ PN,ω(∆n = 0 for every n ∈ [εN,N]∩N) = 0 P(dω)-almost surely?
